catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted from the ideas-to-life-cas repository, a Continuous Architecture System (CAS) CLI runner. The extraction is based on the repository tree, manifests, and key symbols; full source files beyond those listed were not reviewed.
analysis_limits: No full source files were reviewed, only manifests, key-file symbols, and the directory tree.
Runtime traces and execution logs were not inspected; observed state structures are inferred from file layout.
Agent definitions are primarily manifest-level (README, CLAUDE.md, skills), with limited behavioural code inspected.

system_map.overview: CAS is a continuous-architecture harness in which a centralised FlowRunner executes multi-step, context-passing pipelines driven by LLM calls through a provider-agnostic client. Agent capabilities are packaged as reusable skills and constrained by a governance engine, a compliance engine, transition-based action logic, an independent verifier, and persistent knowledge-base state.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Central orchestration agent that steps through pipeline stages, maintains a shared execution context, and coordinates LLM-driven and governance actions.

agents.name: Verifier Agent
agents.role: Independent reviewer that validates agent-proposed changes against architectural rules and acceptance criteria.

agents.name: Governance Action Engine
agents.role: Decision component that interprets rule context and transition registries to restrict or guide allowable governance transitions.

agents.name: Capability Skills
agents.role: Packaged, reusable agent capabilities for feature addition, module refactoring, diagram generation, knowledge-link refactoring, and architecture-review synchronisation.

orchestration.description: FlowRunner is the primary orchestrator, chaining sequential steps that pass a mutable shared context. External GitHub Actions workflows trigger and monitor CAS phases, while governance and compliance engines gate transitions and validate outputs.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLM client
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provider-agnostic LLM invocation so agent steps can switch models without changing pipeline logic.

tools_and_integrations.name: Mock LLM client
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Deterministic, offline LLM replacement for repeatable evaluations and pipeline tests.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetry
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Trace and instrument execution for observing agent pipelines and diagnosing failures.

tools_and_integrations.name: GitHub Actions workflows
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Trigger continuous-architecture, validation, steering-sync, skill-eval, and portal-publish pipelines.

tools_and_integrations.name: Knowledge base filesystem
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Persistent blackboard for decisions, rules, patterns, signals, maps, models, narratives, and project records.

state_and_memory.description: Mutable execution context passed through FlowRunner steps, carrying current pipeline progress and intermediate results.
Curated knowledge base storing architecture decisions, rules, maps, patterns, narratives, and project records for cross-run memory.
Governance inventory, compliance findings, health status, and metrics computed from current repository state and rule evaluation.
Runtime traces, execution profiles, and rule-context snapshots support post-hoc analysis and deterministic governance context.

patterns.name: Shared blackboard execution context

tool_protocols.notes: No explicit tool-calling protocol observed in key symbols.

optimisation_targets.notes: Mutable shared context reduces re-fetching and keeps pipeline steps coherent.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: FlowRunner serialises steps to keep context mutation predictable.

patterns.summary: FlowRunner advances through steps by mutating a single shared context object that carries progress to the next stage.
patterns.intent: Keep multi-step agent work coherent without building complex per-step repositories.
patterns.context: CAS is built as a runner that must perform several related LLM and governance actions in a defined order.
patterns.solution: A central FlowRunner owns a mutable context object and passes it through each sequential step, allowing later steps to see and refine earlier outcomes.
implementation_signals: Central runner class owning flow state
Steps invoked with the same context object

evidence.note: FlowRunner is the orchestrator that drives the pipeline and would naturally own the shared context.
CLI entry point delegates to runner, implying all pipeline stages share one top-level execution context.

benefits: Single source of truth for current pipeline state
costs: Ordering is implicit and must be preserved
Concurrent steps are harder to add
failure_modes: Context bloat leads to accidental coupling
Mutation order bugs if a step is skipped

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when agent steps are tightly related and must share intermediate results, but revisit if the pipeline grows parallel branches.

patterns.name: Provider-agnostic LLM client with deterministic fallback

tool_protocols.notes: Client abstraction, not tool-calling protocol, is the focus.

optimisation_targets.notes: Supports model switching and offline test determinism.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Abstracts model choice so the agent remains simple and portable.

patterns.summary: LLM calls are made through a thin client interface with both a real LiteLLM implementation and a mock implementation, keeping agent logic independent of the underlying model provider.
patterns.intent: Avoid coupling agent steps to a particular LLM provider or service.
patterns.context: CAS must support varied model providers and also run deterministically in CI/evaluations.
forces: Costs and latency differ across providers
patterns.solution: Define a common LLM client contract, provide a LiteLLM-backed implementation for real use, and a mock implementation for deterministic execution.
implementation_signals: Separate lite client and mock client modules
Both classes expose the same interface
LiteLLM dependency configured as a project dependency

evidence.note: Deterministic client for offline and evaluation runs.
LiteLLM is the configured provider access layer.

benefits: Model upgrades without touching agent logic
costs: Client contract must be kept stable
failure_modes: Interface drift if mocks lag real client

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse in any LLM-driven pipeline that needs provider portability and test determinism.

patterns.name: Rule-based compliance gate on agent outputs

tool_protocols.notes: No MCP or tool-calling; governance is procedural.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures agent-generated changes respect architecture rules.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Allows agent autonomy but applies an explicit rule gate before acceptance.

patterns.summary: A ComplianceEngine evaluates agent-produced artifacts against governance rules and produces compliance findings that must be resolved before changes are accepted.
patterns.intent: Prevent autonomous agent actions from silently violating architecture rules.
patterns.context: CAS produces/refines architecture knowledge and code changes that could drift from the project's intended architecture.
patterns.solution: ComplianceEngine collects compliance findings and metrics, which downstream governance actions use to block or remediate non-compliant results.

evidence.note: Central engine that checks agent outputs against rules.

costs: Overly strict rules can slow agents
Compliance engine can become a bottleneck
failure_modes: Rules not covering new artifact types

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply when agent outputs alter governed artefacts and rules need to be enforced automatically.

patterns.name: Transition-registry governance actions

tool_protocols.notes: No tool protocol; state transitions are explicit data structures.

optimisation_targets.notes: Constrains agent actions to known valid transitions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents can act, but only through registered, permitted state transitions.

patterns.summary: GovernanceActionEngine uses a TransitionRegistry to limit agent-driven governance changes to explicitly allowed state transitions.
patterns.intent: Prevent arbitrary governance mutations by requiring actions to fit a known transition set.
patterns.context: CAS must promote findings, decisions, and learning artifacts without allowing the agent to mutate governance state unchecked.
forces: Need to keep governance model explicit
patterns.solution: A transition registry enumerates valid state changes; GovernanceActionEngine resolves requested actions against it and only emits valid GovernanceActions.

evidence.note: Explicit transition registry and action resolver.

costs: Transition registry must be kept up to date
New governance paths require code changes
May be too rigid for exploratory agent work
failure_modes: Missing transition records are hard to debug

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when autonomous agents mutate stateful governance/architecture data and you need safe, auditable transitions.

patterns.name: Skill-packaged agent capabilities

evidence.note: Multiple skill directories represent distinct task-oriented sub-agent capabilities.

tool_protocols.notes: Skills define task boundaries, not protocol-level tools.

optimisation_targets.notes: Packaging recurring tasks as skills makes agent reuse and consistency easier.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Skills constrain agent work to known task templates.

patterns.summary: Recurring agent tasks are packaged as skill directories (e.g., add-or-modify-feature, refactor-module, drawio-generator) so the flow runner or assistant can invoke a known, repeatable capability.
patterns.intent: Turn repeated agent operations into well-scoped, reusable capabilities.
patterns.context: The repository contains many specialised agent skills that need to remain discoverable and maintainable.
patterns.solution: Each skill lives in its own directory with instructions/resources; the same skills are mirrored in .agents and .claude so different assistant runtimes can use them.

evidence.note: Skill evaluation workflow validates skill behaviour.

costs: Need to keep skill contracts up to date

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse as a general way to package agent capabilities for a specific domain, keeping each skill atomic and testable.

patterns.name: Independent verifier agent

tool_protocols.notes: Verifier is a role-level reviewer, not a tool invocation protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Adds an independent check before agent output is accepted.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Autonomy is balanced with a separate, controlled acceptance review.

patterns.summary: A dedicated verifier subagent reviews agent-produced changes, providing an independent quality check in addition to the production agent.
patterns.intent: Reduce the risk of a producer agent accepting its own flawed output.
patterns.context: CAS runs agentic changes that affect architecture knowledge and code; verification is separated into a distinct role.
forces: Agent outputs can be subtly wrong
patterns.solution: Define a verifier subagent (in both .claude/agents and .agents/subagents) that runs as a second opinion on agent outputs, supported by validation workflows.
implementation_signals: Verifier appears in both agent runtimes

evidence.note: Mirrored verifier subagent for the other runtime.

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt when agent outputs are high-impact and independent review is worth the added latency.

patterns.name: Managed steering approval workflow

evidence.note: Workflow synchronises steering state across agent runs.

tool_protocols.notes: Approval is carried through workflow state and persistent steering records.

optimisation_targets.notes: Keeps human/system steering decisions in charge of agent autonomy.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents can act, but steering sync provides a control point for governance direction.

patterns.summary: CAS uses a managed steering-sync workflow and persistent steering records to keep agentic work aligned with human-approved architecture direction.
patterns.intent: Ensure agentic architecture changes do not silently diverge from approved steering decisions.
patterns.context: Continuous-architecture runs must reconcile with a steerable governance agenda and promotion decisions.
forces: Need a durable record of decisions
patterns.solution: A dedicated GitHub Action syncs managed steering state, and promotion/decision templates persist approved governance moves.

benefits: Allows humans to influence autonomous work
failure_modes: Promotion decisions are made without proper review

patterns.reuse_notes: Use in any agentic system that must continuously reconcile autonomous output with an approved human governance agenda.

patterns.name: Persistent knowledge blackboard

optimisation_targets.notes: Gives agents and governance components a shared, persistent frame of reference.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents can read/write shared knowledge but are expected to follow the knowledge taxonomy.

patterns.summary: Architecture knowledge is stored as a persistent filesystem blackboard under cas-knowledge, allowing multiple agent steps and governance components to share decisions, rules, patterns, and signals across runs.
patterns.intent: Give agents durable, structured memory beyond a single pipeline run.
patterns.context: CAS needs to reason about architecture over time and across projects, not just during one LLM call.
forces: Multiple agent roles need shared context
patterns.solution: Use a dedicated filesystem tree with global and project subdirectories for decisions, governance, maps, models, narratives, patterns, rules, and signals.
implementation_signals: Templates and rule contexts around the same tree

evidence.note: Persistent rule context consumed by governance.

costs: Knowledge can go stale if not curated

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any agent system that needs a persistent, inspectable shared memory between runs and roles.

patterns.name: Evidence-driven pattern promotion lifecycle

optimisation_targets.notes: Encourages evidence-backed evolution from heuristic to pattern.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Templates constrain how knowledge is promoted rather than letting agents invent categories.

patterns.summary: CAS treats patterns as a managed lifecycle: observations start as heuristics/learnings and can be promoted to patterns through evidence-backed templates.
patterns.intent: Keep reusable architecture knowledge grounded in evidence rather than ad-hoc insight.
patterns.context: The knowledge base contains templates for pattern, heuristic-to-pattern, learning, and promotion decisions.
patterns.solution: Provide explicit templates for documenting patterns, heuristic-to-pattern transitions, learnings, and promotion decisions, guiding agent output into a governed knowledge flow.
implementation_signals: Separate templates for heuristic-to-pattern and pattern
Global patterns directory next to learnings

evidence.note: Template for promoting heuristics to patterns.

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply in any repository where agent-generated architecture knowledge should mature from observation to reusable pattern through explicit review.

patterns.name: Automated agent-skill evaluation suite

tool_protocols.notes: Evaluation is test-harness based, not a runtime protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Measures skill correctness and regression before real-world use.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Evaluation is codified in assertions and suites, limiting runtime interpretation.

patterns.summary: CAS defines typed skill-evaluation models (assertions, cases, suites, results) and runs them in a GitHub workflow to test agent skill correctness.
patterns.intent: Give skill capabilities a reproducible evaluation harness instead of only manual checks.
patterns.context: Skills are packaged agent capabilities that need automated validation across changes.
forces: Skills can regress with dependency updates
patterns.solution: Model skill evaluations as typed Pydantic structures (assertions, cases, suites, reports) and execute them in a dedicated CI workflow.
implementation_signals: Assertions as part of evaluation model

failure_modes: Evaluation not run on every change

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt when agent capabilities are modular and need regression testing in CI.

patterns.name: CI-embedded agentic orchestration

evidence.note: Workflow triggers CAS pipeline on events.

tool_protocols.notes: CI workflow is the event/trigger mechanism.

optimisation_targets.notes: Makes agentic work repeatable and automatically triggered.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: CI triggers bound when and how agents run, but still leave agent logic mostly autonomous.

patterns.summary: CAS embeds its agentic pipeline into GitHub Actions so continuous-architecture, validation, steering sync, and skill evaluations run on repository events.
patterns.intent: Make the agentic pipeline a normal, observable part of repository automation.
patterns.context: The repository has many CI workflows that trigger CAS phases, including continuous architecture, steering sync, validation, skill evals, and portal publishing.
patterns.solution: Use GitHub Actions to launch and coordinate CAS stages, providing event triggers, environment setup, and external validation.
implementation_signals: Workflow names map to CAS phases
patterns.reuse_notes: Use when agentic pipelines must run alongside normal repository automation and benefit from event-driven scheduling.

patterns.name: Deterministic bootstrap and agent-config synchronisation

evidence.note: Bootstrap merges agent settings and syncs directories.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures agent runtimes consistently see the same configuration.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Configuration is centralised and synchronised rather than left to agent discretion.

patterns.summary: A bootstrap routine merges CAS governance blocks, synchronises Claude settings, and creates symlinks/copies for agent definitions so multiple runtimes behave consistently.
patterns.intent: Reduce runtime drift between different agent environments (Claude, agents) by ensuring they share the same governance and skill configuration.
patterns.context: The repository exposes skills and subagents under both .agents and .claude directories, and has a bootstrap script to initialise workspaces.
patterns.solution: Bootstrap merges governance blocks into a canonical workspace structure, copies or symlinks files, and renders an onboarding checklist.

costs: Bootstrap must be rerun on changes

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when one repository feeds multiple agent runtimes and you need deterministic configuration propagation.

patterns.name: Trace-instrumented agent execution

tool_protocols.notes: Observability is implemented through OpenTelemetry, not agent protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Trace data helps evaluate and debug agent runs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Instrumentation is explicit and separated from agent behaviour.

patterns.summary: CAS depends on OpenTelemetry and persists runtime traces, letting each agent pipeline run be traced and inspected.
patterns.intent: Make agent execution behaviour visible and auditable, especially for governance and evaluation.
patterns.context: Runtime directory contains traces and execution profiles, and pyproject includes OpenTelemetry dependencies.
patterns.solution: Include OpenTelemetry SDK/API and write runtime traces to a traces directory alongside execution profile and rule context.
patterns.reuse_notes: Apply when agentic pipelines need external observability and post-hoc audit of LLM or governance decisions.

patterns.name: Runtime rule-context snapshot

tool_protocols.notes: State is serialised as JSON/YAML files, not an agent protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides a deterministic context for governance and compliance decisions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Rules are captured in a static snapshot rather than inferred at runtime.

patterns.summary: CAS stores runtime rule context and execution profiles as persistent files, giving governance components a stable, reproducible view of the rules in effect for a run.
patterns.intent: Ensure governance/compliance decisions are based on a clear rule context, not on implicit runtime state.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge/runtime contains rule-context.json and execution-profile.yaml alongside traces, which likely feed the governance engine.
forces: Need to trace which rules were used
patterns.solution: Materialise rule context and execution profile in the runtime knowledge tree so any agent/governance run can reference them.

evidence.note: Structured rule context for runtime use.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when governance decisions must be reproducible and traceable to the exact rule set used.

patterns.name: Agentic-system health model

tool_protocols.notes: Health is computed from dashboard model, not an agent protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides a compact summary of how well the agentic governance system is doing.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Health is derived from defined metrics rather than self-assessment.

patterns.summary: CAS computes a health status with reasons from governance and compliance metrics, surfacing a compact signal of system quality.
patterns.intent: Make the state of the agentic architecture process easy to assess at a glance.
patterns.context: The dashboard health model calculates status based on governance data, likely for the portal or CLI.
patterns.solution: A health model converts governance/compliance indicators into a HealthStatus and human-readable health reasons.

costs: Health may lag actual system state

patterns.reuse_notes: Use in agentic governance systems to surface a simple health score from richer governance metrics.

anti_patterns.name: Duplicate agent and skill definitions across runtimes
symptoms: The same verifier and skill definitions appear in both .agents and .claude directories.
Bootstrap code contains merge/sync logic specifically to keep these trees aligned.
Runtime-specific settings differ (Claude settings vs generic subagents).

where_observed.note: Sync/merge logic exists to reconcile duplicates.

impact: Definitions can diverge, causing agents to behave differently across runtimes.
Increased maintenance burden for every skill/subagent change.
Bootstrap failures can silently break one runtime.
suggested_remediation: Keep a single source of truth for skill/subagent definitions and generate/symlink runtime copies.
Add CI checks that diff .agents and .claude definitions.
Prefer symlinks over copies if supported by the target runtime.

anti_patterns.name: Hardcoded CI workflow values
symptoms: A validation script explicitly checks for zero hardcoded values in workflows.
It also checks for unpinned installers and unreachable dry-run conditions.
This suggests past workflows contained hardcoded, environment-specific values.

where_observed.note: Validator targets hardcoded and unpinned CI configuration.

impact: Hardcoded values reduce portability of the agentic pipeline.
Unpinned installers make builds less reproducible.
Debugging failures is harder when values are baked into workflows.
suggested_remediation: Use environment-specific variables and reusable composite actions.
Add linting that bans hardcoded workflow values from CI.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Agent capabilities are codified as skill directories and verifier definitions, while templates standardise knowledge/pattern prompts.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Agent prompts are not written inline in Python but packaged as skill files, making them reviewable as contracts.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Typed skill eval models plus a dedicated skill-eval workflow provide automated evaluation of agent capabilities.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Evaluation is separate from pipeline execution, giving a quality gate before skills are trusted.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: ComplianceEngine, TransitionRegistry, and managed steering sync constrain what autonomous agents can change.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Safety is implemented through explicit rule checks and state transitions rather than sandboxing.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Provider-agnostic LLM client plus mock client allows deterministic, low-cost test/CI runs; CI workflows bound how often full agentic runs happen.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Cost control is primarily achieved by abstracting model choice and enabling deterministic offline evaluation.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: OpenTelemetry dependencies, runtime traces, execution profiles, and health models expose pipeline behaviour.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Observability spans both runtime telemetry and post-hoc dashboard metrics.

open_questions.question: Does FlowRunner expose true parallel execution or is the pipeline strictly serial?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The shared mutable context pattern works well serially but needs fan-out/fan-in handling for parallel agent steps.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Only runner.py#FlowRunner was visible; no step-level execution model was inspected.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Inspect src/cas_runner/runner.py fully and any step/executor modules referenced by FlowRunner.

open_questions.question: Are the .agents and .claude skill definitions generated from a single source of truth or manually duplicated?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If duplicated manually, drift between runtimes is a real maintenance and safety risk.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Bootstrap contains merge/symlink logic, but the source of truth is not visible in the provided tree.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Examine bootstrap.py and any skill-generation workflows to determine whether a canonical definition exists.

open_questions.question: How do GovernanceActionEngine and ComplianceEngine interact with the persistent knowledge blackboard at runtime?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether governance uses the blackboard as source of truth or as a snapshot layer.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Only model/engine symbols were seen, not the read/write calls to cas-knowledge.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Trace data flow from cas-knowledge/runtime/rule-context.json into compliance and action engine code.

open_questions.question: Is there a deterministic replay of agent pipelines based on traces or is tracing only informational?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Could indicate whether retries and rollback are supported when agent steps fail.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Traces exist, but no replay/rollback symbols were observed.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Search for retry, replay, or rollback logic around FlowRunner and governance steps.
